# GitHub Issue #396

## Title
pit/durable: collapse finished runs' tool calls to their labels after each run

## Description
## Problem

On pi-durable hosts, a conversation keeps every tool call and result in context until pi-durable's threshold compaction runs. pi-action threads are where this costs the most:

- They are linear and long-lived.
- Follow-up comments arrive minutes to days apart, so every follow-up starts with a cold prompt cache and re-sends the whole thread.
- They run headless, so nobody follows Pit's context-pressure notices.

Measured on `refs/pi/threads/383` (one pi-action run, 140 model-visible entries):

| | Bytes |
|---|---|
| 70 `pi.tool-result` entries | 744 KB (largest 74 KB) |
| 69 `pi.assistant` entries, mostly program source | 266 KB |
| Final answers (assistant entries without tool calls) | 5 KB |

The run's 69 model requests read 7.4M tokens from the cache, and the prompt peaked at 171K tokens. The system prompt, tools and catalogs are 41K of that; the rest is mostly old tool calls and results.

The idea comes from [UniiChat](https://github.com/VictorTaelin/UniiChat)'s memory tree. It keeps every message forever but shows the model a bounded view in which finished messages are one-line summaries, and the model can zoom back to any original. UniiChat pays a second model to write those lines. **Pit doesn't need one: the main model has already written them.**

1. Every `typescript` call carries a label the model writes (the `// @pit:` header or the `label` argument). All 70 calls in thread #383 had one, for example "Load delivery skill and inspect repo state" and "Read global-documentation source".
2. `present.result` (`src/durable/present.ts`) already works out each result's injected functions, whether it succeeded, and the error's first line, deterministically.
3. The run's final answer is the model's own summary of what it learned, and it is already protected from edits.
4. Notes (`setNote`) carry working state across compactions.

Collapsing each finished call and its results to one deterministic line would bring thread #383's 70 calls down from about 1 MB to about 21 KB (around 300 bytes each). A follow-up would then start at about 47K tokens instead of about 170K. There is no model call, so the edit can be retried safely after a crash and the next run never waits on summaries.

## Proposal

Add an automatic collapse to the `afterRun` path that already applies staged edits (`APPLY_STAGED_EDITS_HOOK` and `APPLY_STAGED_EDITS` in `src/durable/context/apply.ts`).

### When

- In `afterRun`, collapse the tool calls of finished runs older than the newest `keepRuns` runs (default `1`). A follow-up usually refers to the run just before it, so that run stays whole and older ones collapse.
- The rewrite happens once per run, at a point where pi-action's next request is cold anyway.
- Optional floor `minTokens`: collapse only once the active context passes that many tokens, so short threads stay verbatim. Choose a default and justify it in the PR, for example 32K.

### What

- Only assistant tool calls and their results, using the same pairing as Pit's existing `elide` of a tool-calling entry. The assistant entry keeps its text and its thinking (signatures included). Its tool calls and their results become one plain-text note, so no call is left unanswered and no result is orphaned.
- Never touch:
  - user and host messages, and pi-action comments;
  - assistant text and answers;
  - notes and compaction summaries;
  - entries already elided, summarized or with a staged edit;
  - the current run;
  - an entry no larger than its note.
- Calls of any tool may collapse. Use the label and outcome for `typescript`, and the tool name and outcome for others.

### The line

Extend `callNote` (`src/durable/context/edits.ts`) so a collapsed call reads like:

```
[Pit: collapsed typescript call · "Read npm and git global and command sources" · workspace.read, workspace.search · ok · ~18.2K tokens · original: session.inspectEntry("212")]
```

- The label: header or `label` argument, else the program's first line, as `present.call` already resolves it.
- The injected functions, from the same parsing `present.result` uses.
- `ok`, or `failed: <error's first line>`, bounded.
- Token size, and the `inspectEntry` IDs of the call and every result.
- Bound each line, for example to 512 bytes, and say in the PR what is cut first.

### How it's written

- One write per `afterRun`. The automatic collapses and any edits the model staged during the run go together in the single `pit.context-edit` entry, with provenance that tells automatic collapses apart from the model's (for example `operation: "collapse"`), so `session.outline()` and the transcript can show them.
- pi-durable entries stay append-only, and `session.inspectEntry` still returns every original.
- A failed or aborted run collapses nothing, the same as the existing staged-edit behaviour.

### Configuration

- `PitDurableOptions.collapse?: { keepRuns?: number; minTokens?: number } | false`.
- The default needs a decision in the PR. Either make it on by default for pi-durable hosts and list it as a behaviour change in the release notes, or make it opt-in for one release. I lean towards on by default, since pi-action is the main durable host and is headless.
- Pi (the main extension) is out of scope: leave `src/context/` alone.

### Prompt

Add a durable-only guideline to Pit's durable sections, for example:

> Calls from finished runs collapse to their labels: give each call a specific label, and say in your answer what a later run will need.

Collapsed lines are only as good as their labels.

## Edge cases

- **Two assistant messages in a row.** A collapsed call can leave two assistant messages adjacent. `docs/durable.md` notes the prototype only checked pi-ai's faux provider. Verify a strict provider, either Anthropic via the NVIDIA/Bedrock route pi-action uses or Anthropic directly, accepts the collapsed context. If it doesn't, merge adjacent texts or choose a different shape, and document what you chose.
- **Compaction.** The collapse must not cross pi-durable's newest compaction head. Entries before the head aren't in context.
- **Forks and children.** A fork inherits the collapsed view from its fork point. Collapsing in the parent afterwards must not affect the fork.
- **Terminating runs.** A run that ended because a call asked to `terminate` (`reason: "terminate"`, for example `ui.input` posting a question) counts as a finished run.
- **Idempotence.** Re-running the task after a crash must not collapse an entry twice or fail on one that is already collapsed.
- **Model-staged edits on the same entries.** The model's explicit `elide`/`summarize` wins, and the collapse skips those targets.

## Tests

Follow the [pit-test-audit](https://github.com/cv/pit/blob/main/.pi/skills/pit-test-audit/SKILL.md) gate and assert on what the model sees next, using the real pi-durable harness in `test/durable/`:

- Three runs with `keepRuns: 1`: after the third run, the first two runs' calls are collapsed lines, and the third run's calls and every answer and user message are verbatim. `inspectEntry` returns each original.
- `minTokens` above the context size: nothing collapses.
- A failed or aborted run: nothing collapses, and its staged edits drop, as now.
- A model `elide` staged in the same run lands in the same edit entry, and the collapse skips its targets.
- An already collapsed entry isn't collapsed again when the task is re-run.
- A table of line formats: labelled `typescript` call, unlabelled call (the program's first line), failed call (the error's first line), non-`typescript` tool, and a call with several results. Include the byte bound.
- `collapse: false` changes nothing.
- Run `tests.probeMutation` on the `keepRuns` boundary and on the protection of answers and user messages.

## Acceptance

This changes what pi-durable hosts send the model, so per AGENTS.md: open the PR with `Refs` (not `Closes`), merge it, release it, and point pi-assistant at the new tag. Then, on a real pi-action thread:

1. A follow-up on a thread with at least two earlier runs shows the older runs' calls as collapsed lines in the request (check the thread's stored entries and `session.outline()`), and its first request's prompt is much smaller than before.
2. The strict provider accepts that collapsed context.
3. The model can still get a collapsed result back with `session.inspectEntry` when the follow-up needs it.

Only then close this issue.

## Out of scope

- Pi (the main extension).
- Hierarchical merging of collapsed lines (UniiChat's tree). pi-durable's own threshold compaction remains the backstop. A later issue could supply its summary deterministically from the collapsed lines through `beforeCompact`.
- The 41K-token fixed prompt (system, tools, catalogs), which deserves its own issue.

---

@pi please implement this as a new PR. Use `Refs` for this issue, not `Closes`, since acceptance needs a release and a live pi-action thread. Pick the defaults, explain them in the PR, and report what the strict-provider check showed.

## Your Reply

pi-action posts your final response as a comment on this issue or pull request. **Do not post your reply yourself**, for example with `gh issue comment`, `gh pr comment`, `gh pr review`, or `gh api`. That would post the same answer twice. Use `gh` to comment only where the task asks for it, such as on another issue.

## Important: Artifact and Script Requirements

**CRITICAL:** After the GitHub Action finishes running, all files modified or created are lost, and the GitHub Action runner is destroyed. Therefore:

1. **All generated code and artifacts MUST be committed** - Any files you create, modify, or generate must be committed and pushed to the repository before the action completes. Nothing will persist otherwise.

2. **Any throw-away scripts generated MUST be run immediately** - If you create temporary scripts (like `/tmp/create-issues.sh` or similar), you must execute them during the same session. They will be lost when the runner terminates.

3. **Commit and push all work** - Always end your work by committing and pushing changes to ensure they persist beyond the GitHub Action execution.
